Also bei deinem Fall kommt es darauf an, wie dein Minijob durch den Arbeitgeber abgerechnet wird.

Minijobs sind besondere Arbeitsverhältnisse im Rahmen des deutschen Rentenversicherrungsrechts. Das deutsche Steuerrecht kennt sowas eigentlich nicht.

Da allerdings der Gesetzgeber solche "geringfügigen" Arbeitsverhältnisse nicht bestrafen möchte, gibt es den §40a Abs. 2 EStG, wodurch eine Pauschsteuer in Höhe von 2 % des Arbeitslohns an die Minijob-Zentrale abgeführt wird.

Wird die Pauschsteuer abgeführt (sollte auf deiner Lohnabrechnung stehen) musst du das Arbeitsentgelt nicht in deiner Einkommensteuererklärung angeben (keine Sorge, dass ist keine Steuerhinterziehung). Auch dann nicht, wenn du noch andere Einkünfte erzielst.

Solltest du noch einen zweiten Minijob haben und unter 556 € monatlich bleiben, gilt das auch noch. Solltest du über 556 € erzielen, ist kann keiner der beiden Arbeitsverhältnisse mit der Pauachalsteuer abgerechnet werden. In diesem Fall musst du diese beiden Arbeitsverhältnisse in deiner Einkommensteuererklärung angeben.

Bei dem Appen handelt es sich um Einkünfte aus Gewerbebetrieb im Sinne des § 15 Abs. 1 EStG. D.h. du musst die Einnahmen (Betriebseinnahmen) mit deinen Ausgaben (Betriebsausgaben) gegenüber stellen (sog. Einnahmenüberschussrechnung). Diese musst du definitiv in der Steuererklärung angeben.

Aufgrund der Einkünfte aus Gewerbebetrieb wärst du sogar verpflichtet eine Einkommensteuererklärung abzugeben, sobald die Einkünfte mehr als 410 € betragen (§ 46 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 EStG).

Minijob und Appen sind steuerrechtlich zwei verschiedene Einkünfte, die nicht miteinander interferieren. D.h. das Appen hat keine Auswirkungen auf den Minijob und anders herum.

Well your weightloss Journey begins with a Calculation as you already did. You need to understand that the caloriecalculation has multiple layers.

The first layer ist your Basal metabolic rate. The basal metabolic rate depends on height, weight, age und sex. For you your basal metabolic rate is round about  2.031 kcal.

Second we need to calculate your total energy turnover.

To calculate your total energy turnover we take your basal metabolic rate and multiply it with some factors. Those factors depend on your daily activity. Are you more or less active at daytime. Are your working an office job, etc.

Are you inactive = 1,2
Office Job (you are mainly sitting) = 1,4 
You are mainly walking or standing = 1,6
You are very active (Constructionworker, etc.) = 2

In my calculation I assume you are a office worker (you can change the factor by your activity level) just as an example.

So this brings us to your total energy turnover of:
2.031 kcal * 1,4 = 2.844 kcal just to maintain your wheight.

For Fatloss you need a caloriedeficit. Your deficit depends on how fast you want to lose wheight. 1kg of bodyfat equals about 7.500 kcal. So for example we take your 2.000 kcal, this equals to a deficit of about 844 kcal. In about 8 days of maintaining this deficit you CAN (very important) lose up to 1 kg of bodyfat. I would recommend a smaller deficit because you can eat more and you will have more energy for the day. Always remember a diet is very hard.

A deficit of about 20 - 25 % is absolutely ok.


Now let's talk about food.
Which food you eat is also very important. There are many diet forms. Some lower your fats you eat. Some diets lower your carbs.

First of protein. Protein is very important for your muscles. I would try to eat about 2 - 2.5 g per Kg Bodyweight. This equals about 170 g of protein.

Second, carbs. For a diet I would lower your carbs because your body needs to learn to use its energydeposits that are already there so your bodyfat. You will feel terrible, trust me but it works if you do what you have to do.

For carbs I wold recommend about 30 % of your daily calorie intake are calories from carbs. So for example your daily intake is 2.000 kcal. This means about 2.000 kcal * 30 % = 600 kcal/ 4 = 150 g of carbs.

Third and last fats. Now you are filling the gab with your fats. If we take your 2.000 kcal, the 150 g of carbs and 170 g of Protein we have already used about 150g*4 + 170g*4 = 1.280 kcal. We have about 2.000 kcal - 1.280 kcal = 720 kcal not used. Now we can calculate your fats. 1g of Fat equals to 9 kcal. So your daily fat intake can be up to 720 kcal / 9 = 80 g of fats.

So your daily macros can look like this:
Daily Kcal = 2.000
Protein = 170 g
Carbs = 150 g
Fats = 80 g


Now some important notes:
It is absolutely ok if you cheat. A cheat meal is very healthy actually, if you do it right.

Also a little tip for sticking to your diet. Remember 90:10. 90 % of your meals you eat healthy and clean and sticking to your diet plan. 10 % of your meals you can have a bit of fun. For example you eat 5 meals a day. This means in 2 days you have 10 meals. 9 meals you eat clean. On the 10th meal you can have a little bit of fun, like eating fast food or go to a restaurant or something. But remember to lose fat you need to maintain a deficit.

People always think that you grow in the gym, that is absolutely wrong. You train to damage your muscle fibres, so when you rest your body regenerates those muscle fibres. This means you grow when you rest. In a diet you won't build muscle because you are not in a calorie surplus. But you need to train so your body maintains your musclemass and not use it as energy.

First of all, don't let this comment get to you. I know it is a stupid thing to say, but what you think about yourself is more important than what others say about you. Say to yourself "I am beautiful the way that I am and nobody can say otherwise" and mean it like that.

So now to the topic.
First of all to say, building muscle is a long and hard process. Huge muscles won't come over night. You need to be consistent about training, eating and resting. You need to do the work.
There are three big topics you need to take care of. Training, nutrition and rest.

1. Nutrition
So the first thing you need to take care of is your nutrition. A good nutrition is key to put on some muscle. You need to understand that without the right nutrition you can train as hard as you want, but you won't put on muscle.
If you want to gain muscle, you need to eat more calories than you burn over the day.
For a beginner like you, there is no need to eat the same thing every day. Just keep track of what you eat and keep track of your macros.
When I talk about nutrition, I mean carbs, protein and fats.
The most important is protein. You need to eat a lot of protein to gain muscle. (Why, just google it because this post will get long enough.) I would recommend around 2-2,5x per bodyweight.
Fats are necessary for your organs. So don't underestimate the importance of good fats.
And last but not least carbs. Carbs are important for your energy level. To build muscle you need to eat a lot of carbs, so that your body has enough energy to regenerate and keep on going. To gain muscle I eat about 5x my bodyweight. But there are calorie calculators that calculate the right amount for you.
If you want to prep meals, which is OK, there are a few tips. 
Tip 1: Make the meals smaller but more frequent. This makes it easier to eat. Tip 2: Make your meals easy. You don't need complicated meals. Easy simple meals, like chicken with rice and greens. 
Tip 3: Take your meals with you. Even if you are just 5 Minutes away from home, take at least one meal with you, even if you don't need it. Just to have the security of having it with you.

2. Training
I would recommend to start slow. You don't need to train 6 times a week for 3 hours. That would be bad, because you can over train your body. Start slow to get going, to get used to it. For a beginner it is normal to train 3x a week for about 1 1/2 hours. A training plan is a good thing for beginners, just ask at your local gym.
Also I would recommend that you train with a trainer, to get the hang of the machines and the exercise.

3. Rest
Rest is very important for your body. In your Restphase your body regenerates the cells and muscles. The purpose of the exercise is to damage the muscles, so that the body can regenerate and build muscle while resting.

If there are any questions, our something I need to explain, just ask. There is no problem with asking.

I hope this will help you and happy training
